transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-02-25 15:00 PST
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Sameer Rao (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood Product), Priya Nair (AtlasMind Head of ML), Marcus Holt (AtlasMind Platform), Zoe Kim (AtlasMind FinOps), Alex Reeve (AtlasMind Security)

Auto-generated Summary (optional):
Redwood gave a console walkthrough focused on per-route usage analytics, cost breakdown and SLO routing/playbook. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for production; main concerns are predictable cost allocation to product routes, latency SLOs for latency-sensitive features, and SOC2/compliance for customer data. Agreed next steps include a benchmark run, pricing send, and security deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: okay, hi everyone thanks for joining, this is lena from Redwood, i'm the a e covering AtlasMind, um i'll hand over to Sameer who will run through the console and some route finance playbooks.
[00:12] Sameer: hey all, yeah thanks lena. quick agenda — console tour (usage + per-route dashboards), cost breakdown examples, routing and SLO policy demo, and then q&a. we'll call out places where you can pin model versions and apply canary rollouts.
[00:28] Priya: sounds good. we're mostly interested in two things — accounting per product feature (search vs assistant vs summarization) and keeping tail latency under 200ms for our live assistant.
[00:38] Marcus: and we need clear cost allocation to product teams, so finance can charge back accurately.
[00:44] Zoe: yep and also monthly forecasts — we need to understand how bursts impact unit economics.
[00:50] Sameer: understood. quick question — what are your current qps and biggest prompt sizes?
[00:56] Priya: peak ~800 qps across all features, but assistant feature is around 200 qps and has some 3k token prompts, search is shorter. these are ballpark numbers.
[01:10] Sameer: okay that's helpful. i'll show the usage explorer first — you can filter by route (we call them routes, some customers call them features), model, and time window. on the left side you see per-route token counts, per-token cost, and a cost trend chart.
[01:26] (screen share noise)
[01:32] Sameer: for demo data i loaded a sandbox with three routes: assistant-live, docs-search, and summarizer-batch. assistant-live shows higher tail latency and higher CPU/GPU time due to long seq lengths. you can drill into sequence length distribution which is important for kernel selection and batching.
[01:50] Priya: sequence length distribution? can you expand that?
[01:53] Sameer: yeah so the chart shows P50/P90/P99 token lengths per route — for assistant-live your P99 is 2.8k tokens which explains longer runtimes. that points to either moving assistant-live to a dedicated pool with larger kv cache or enabling prefix caching for repeated context.
[02:12] Marcus: dedicated pool costs more but gives consistent latency, right? what's the trade off?
[02:17] Sameer: correct. hosted gives elastic capacity and lower ops, but you may see more variability under burst. dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity, predictable latency and throughput; cost model is monthly commitment plus overage. we can show a forecast with your peak qps.
[02:32] Zoe: can the console show cost per route broken down by model variant and quantization?
[02:37] Sameer: yes — when you click a route, the cost panel splits by model, by quantization profile (gptq/8-bit/4-bit) if used, and by execution mode (streaming vs non-streaming). you can export a CSV.
[02:52] Priya: nice. do you have an example where routing can fallback to cheaper variant automatically?
[02:56] Sameer: i'll demo policy rules next — you can set routing rules with priorities: try high-quality model first (pinned) and fallback to cheaper quantized variant when latency SLO or cost cap is hit. we also have time-of-day policies and region preferences.
[03:11] Alex: quick security question — how is data handled for hosted inference? is input stored, how long, and is that configurable?
[03:19] Diego: good question. for hosted default, we retain logs/inputs for 30 days for debugging and analytics, but enterprise customers can opt out or enable private deployment where logs never leave your VPC and you manage retention. we integrate with KMS and HSM for keys and offer audit logs.
[03:35] Alex: do you have SOC2 and ISO docs?
[03:37] Lena: yep we'll share SOC2 report and our compliance pack — that's in the next steps.
[03:42] Marcus: ok, show us the SLO routing playbook.
[03:45] Sameer: sure — switching to the routing UI. here you define policies: latency target, cost cap per route, and fallback chains. example: assistant-live has latency SLO 200ms; if p95 > 200ms for rolling 5 minutes we route to dedicated-pool or fallback to assistant-lite model. the console also shows simulated impact on monthly cost when you change the policy.
[04:10] Priya: simulated cost — is that accurate? we need to trust the forecast.
[04:14] Sameer: simulation uses historical usage patterns, token mixes and your configured model profiles — it's a forecast not a guarantee but close within ~10-15% in our experience. for high-confidence you can run a short canary and we collect real telemetry to refine the projection.
[04:31] Zoe: can we attribute cost to internal teams automatically?
[04:34] Sameer: yes — you can tag routes with team ids and export chargeback reports weekly — the chargeback export can be piped to your billing system.
[04:42] (small pause)
[04:46] Priya: you mentioned prefix caching earlier — how much does that save for assistant?
[04:50] Sameer: in our tests with repeated context, prefix/KV caching reduced per-request GPU compute by ~30-60% depending on hit rate. there's a tradeoff on memory usage in the dedicated pool.
[05:02] Marcus: what about batch summarizer? we run nightly batches of large documents — can we use cheaper quantized instances?
[05:08] Sameer: absolutely — you can mark routes as batch and schedule them on lower-cost pools; the console can run a suggested quantization profile (we recommend 4-bit for batch, check quality via evals) and show expected quality delta.
[05:21] Priya: any gotchas with quantization and hallucination increases?
[05:25] Diego: yes, smaller quantization may slightly impact some tasks. Redwood Optimize provides per-route evals and regression alerts — you can pin baseline prompt sets to detect quality drift when changing quantization.
[05:38] Alex: encryption at rest and in flight?
[05:40] Sameer: TLS in flight; at rest we use customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and optional CMEK for hosted. logs/audit trails are available centrally or forwarded into your SIEM.
[05:52] Zoe: from finance perspective, show me how a sudden 3x burst affects the monthly bill.
[05:56] Sameer: switching to the cost simulator — i'll inject a burst scenario and you can see month-over-month delta. (simulator shows a spike graph) with hosted and no reserved cap, the bill bumps ~40% that month; with dedicated reserved capacity sized for peak, cost delta is much smaller but baseline is higher.
[06:20] Marcus: hmm, would dedicated be overkill if our peak is short-lived?
[06:24] Sameer: we often suggest hybrid — baseline on Dedicated and overflow to Hosted with policy-based fallback. that keeps latency tight for steady traffic and lets you absorb spikes without huge reserved commits.
[06:36] Priya: can we test this hybrid approach in our sandbox?
[06:38] Lena: yes — we'll set up a trial with a dedicated pool sized for your P95 and allow overflow to hosted. Sameer will run the benchmarks.
[06:45] (transcription note: brief cross talk)
[06:52] Sameer: i'll also point out the per-route usage timeline — you can correlate config changes to cost and latency trends to tune policies. here's an example where we rolled a quantized model and the console flagged a quality regression on the summarizer route.
[07:06] Priya: show me the alerting — we want to avoid silent regressions.
[07:09] Sameer: alerts can be tied to evals/quality metrics and telemetry thresholds; we send to slack/pagerduty and also create a ticket in your tracker via webhook.
[07:20] Zoe: ok question on chargeback — are there labels you recommend to keep accounting simple?
[07:24] Diego: best practice is route_name + team + cost_center, keep names consistent. Redwood Console has templates for common schemes and we can export a mapping.
[07:33] Marcus: how do you handle model upgrades? we can't afford regressions mid-quarter.
[07:37] Sameer: canary rollouts: keep old model pinned, roll percent traffic to new model and run golden prompt sets for quality. if regression crossed threshold we automatically roll back. you can also schedule upgrades during low-traffic windows.
[07:51] Priya: good. what's the onboarding like?
[07:54] Lena: we do a short pilot — you provide sample traffic and prompts, we run a bench and configure console dashboards and routing rules. usually 2–4 weeks for pilot.
[08:04] Alex: from security: what about egress controls on hosted?
[08:08] Diego: we can restrict external egress from private deployments; for hosted we support network allowlists and IP ranges; enterprise can use VPC peering for restricted connections.
[08:18] (prompted by customer)
[08:22] Marcus: any third-party integrations for cost reporting? we use internal FinOps tools.
[08:26] Sameer: exports are JSON/CSV and we have a small API to pull route-level cost and token metrics; some customers build an ingestion that maps to internal cost models.
[08:36] Zoe: do you track per-token actual GPU time to attribute cost?
[08:40] Sameer: yes — runtime logs capture per-request GPU-ms and token counts; cost is allocated using model profiles that map runtime to unit cost.
[08:50] Priya: let's talk SLA — we need 99.9% for critical assistant route.
[08:55] Lena: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we can include SLO targets in the contract for the dedicated pool. hosted has best-effort SLAs and options for premium tiers.
[09:06] Alex: any independent benchmarks or published performance profiles?
[09:09] Sameer: we have a model catalog with Redwood-verified performance profiles and public benchmark docs; we'll share the link after.
[09:17] (customer asks about competitors)
[09:20] Priya: we've evaluated some other vendors and also considered running our own inference; curious where Redwood shines here.
[09:26] Sameer: main differentiation is the unified console + routing + cost controls — plus production-grade runtime optimizations like continuous batching and KV cache management. self-hosting means you build the orchestration and observability, which adds ops burden.
[09:40] Zoe: can we export route-level chargebacks in a format our ERP consumes?
[09:44] Diego: yes — CSV with cost_center and tags, or push via API.
[09:48] (short silence)
[09:51] Priya: okay time for wrap — this is useful.
[09:54] Lena: recap of next steps — Sameer to run latency/cost benchmarks with your sample payloads, Lena to send pricing and SOC2 packet, schedule security deep dive. any final Qs?
[10:06] Marcus: not right now — we'll follow up in email about dates.
[10:09] Zoe: thanks everyone.
[10:11] Lena: thanks team.

End of transcript.
